quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When you stop your motorcycle with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride faster than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to respond. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing down earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect a rider's ability to ride safely?

options.text: One
Two
Three

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What does it mean for a motorcycle to fit you?

options.text: Your fingertips barely reach the handlebars when sitting.
The seat is one foot higher than your waist when standing next to it.
Your feet comfortably touch the ground when sitting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet comfortably touch the ground when sitting.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you if your feet comfortably reach the ground while you sit on it. Always make sure a motorcycle fits before riding.

questions.question: When should a group of motorcyclists NOT use a staggered formation?

options.text: It should always be used.
When entering or exiting a highway.
When riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering or exiting a highway.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation most of the time. Switch to single-file when riding in curves, turning, entering, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What gear should your motorcycle be in when starting the engine?

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that shows when you are in neutral.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop behind it on the roadway.
Stop and wait for it to move.
Move to a different lane away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from it.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give an emergency vehicle extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop when approaching an emergency scene.

questions.question: Which is NOT a potential problem while riding?

options.text: A change in road surface coming up.
Traffic around you.
Conditions that stay the same as you approach.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that stay the same as you approach.
questions.explanation: Look ahead for problems on the roadway and make a plan to reduce their risks.

questions.question: What happens when you grab the front brake or jam the rear brake?

options.text: The brakes can lock.
It is the best way to stop in an emergency.
It is the best way to slow down on wet streets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes can lock.
questions.explanation: Grabbing the front brake or jamming the rear brake can cause the brakes to lock. This can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: What tire pressure adjustment is likely needed when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Reduce the tire pressure.
Make no adjustment.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Add a few pounds of pressure to your tires before riding with a passenger. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.

questions.question: What angle should a parked motorcycle make with the curb?

options.text: Between 45 and 90 degrees.
No wheel or fender should touch the curb.
Parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at an angle between 45 and 90 degrees to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on this sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find an alternate route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They provide a more narrow view of the road.
They provide a wider view of the road.
They provide a better view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They provide a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles coming toward you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: May be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for the driver and passenger
Are not required

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests to stay balanced. Your motorcycle must have footrests for both the driver and passenger. Good footing keeps your passenger from falling off and pulling you down too.

questions.question: When riding in a group, mirrors:

options.text: Should be checked frequently by all riders.
Should be used only by the lead rider.
Should not be checked frequently because they can be a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked frequently by all riders.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, all riders should check their mirrors often. This helps you watch the riders behind you and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a passenger vehicle's brake light.

options.text: More noticeable than
Just as noticeable as
Not as noticeable as

questions.correctAnswerText: Not as noticeable as
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle's brake light is usually harder to see than a larger vehicle's brake light. This is especially true when your taillight is on. Other drivers may not see your brake light, so be careful.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that traffic is merging.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Your mirrors can adequately show you your surroundings.
Do a head check in addition to using your mirrors.
Activate your turn signal and immediately move to the right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do a head check in addition to using your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, in addition to using your mirrors.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a way to control a motorcycle in a turn?

options.text: Accelerate through the turn.
Reduce your speed before turning.
Lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate through the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn safely, slow down before you enter the turn. Look where you want to go, lean your body in that direction, and gently speed up as you go through the turn to keep your balance.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked until you stop.
Keep squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake, then apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake right away. Then apply the brake again with steady, controlled pressure.

questions.question: What is the best way to be seen while riding?

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in low visibility.
Always use your headlight.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to ride with your headlight on at all times.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. This is safest. Riding to the side nearest the passing driver increases collision risk. Riding to the far side may make them return to your lane too early.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you best.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you best.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move into the part of your lane that puts you in other drivers' view as soon as possible.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle passenger sit?

options.text: With their feet on the ground when the motorcycle stops.
Without a back rest.
As far forward as possible without blocking the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: As far forward as possible without blocking the rider.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without blocking the rider. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride at slower speeds than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, ride slower and allow more stopping distance due to added weight. The passenger should hold the motorcycle's passenger handholds or the rider's waist—not the back of the bike.

questions.question: What does the SEE strategy stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy. It stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be more visible. Avoid drab or dark colors while riding.

questions.question: What should you tell a passenger when riding together?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.
Avoid unnecessary talking or movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid unnecessary talking or movement.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move unnecessarily while riding. Passengers should board only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the rider.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols and tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.
